bc_lakeside_in_the_woods.blurb: Lakeside in the Woods is a forested, east-facing crag inside Murrin Park, just south of Squamish, so it gets soft, filtered light in the morning. About 25 routes are spread across trad lines and bolted sport climbs, with the odd top rope and aid line mixed in. The grade spread is wide: a few easy climbs near 5.5 to 5.8, a solid cluster in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, the largest group at 5.11, and a couple of very hard pieces at the top end. Moderate sport routes sit toward the south end, while the hardest and boldest lines are in the middle of the wall. A good pick for a mixed party.

bc_shannon_falls_wall.blurb: Shannon Falls Wall is a slab face beside the waterfall in Shannon Falls Provincial Park, just south of the Chief near Squamish. Most of its 25 routes are trad, many of them following cracks, with a handful of sport lines and a single top rope. Expect everything from short single pitches to longer multi-pitch outings, with views over the falls and Howe Sound. Grades run from about 5.7 to 5.12: a few at 5.8 and 5.9, a good block at 5.10, and the biggest group at 5.11, so it leans toward climbers comfortable on gear and on stout grades.

bc_maternal_wall.blurb: Maternal Wall is a bolted sport wall in the Maternal Group at Skaha Bluffs, near Penticton, tucked into a narrow canyon next to Screeching Wall. The climbing is long, blocky and overhanging on good holds, and the lines can feel like a maze that rewards patience and thought. Of 25 routes, nearly all are sport with one trad line. Nothing here is easy: the grades start at 5.10 and gather in the 5.11 and low 5.12 range, which makes it a wall for strong, experienced sport climbers rather than beginners. It faces west, so expect sun later in the day.

bc_the_wave_3.blurb: The Wave is a short, steep, south-facing band among the Southern Crags at Skaha Bluffs near Penticton, looking out over Skaha Lake toward Red Tail. Most of its 24 routes are overhanging sport climbs, plus a few trad lines. This is a place for hard climbing: the bulk of routes are 5.12, with a good number of 5.13s, a few 5.11s and just a couple of 5.9s. The sun makes it a warm option on cool days, though the wall catches some morning shade. Popular lines can get busy, but there are usually other options if you climb 5.11 or 5.12.

bc_b_titanic_south.blurb: Titanic South is a bouldering sector in the Grand Wall Boulders, set in the forest below the Chief at Squamish. It holds about 25 problems across a broad range, from VB and V0 through V5, with a few much harder lines at V7 and V8. The wide spread of easy and moderate problems makes it a friendly stop for a mixed group. The Grand Wall area stays shady and cool in summer, which suits warm days, but landings can be rocky and rooty, so bring extra pads. The area is a maze of trails and boulders, and a topo helps.

bc_o_animal_magnetism.blurb: Animal Magnetism is a bouldering sector within the Grand Wall Boulders at Squamish, sharing a trail with the Heartbreak Hotel area and the Cacodemon Boulder. It has around 24 problems with a very wide spread: a few VB to V1 warm-ups, a strong middle of V2 to V7, and a short tail of difficult problems into double digits. Expect steep, short walls with small edges and sloping lips. The Grand Wall area stays shady and cool in summer, and landings are often rocky and rooty, so bring extra pads. The terrain is a maze, so a topo is worth carrying.

bc_fukushima.blurb: Fukushima is a very large boulder in the Ponderosa boulders, high above Arrow Lake in the West Kootenay, in open ponderosa pine forest. It sits roughly a minute uphill from the smaller Ponderosa Boulder, which makes a handy warm-up. The 24 problems here are big lines on strong holds, and the grades lean hard: one easy problem, a few around V2 to V4, then most between V5 and V9. It is an outing for climbers who already boulder at a solid level, with plenty of variety on one tall, long boulder.
